description_en: Birth of Marcus Junius Brutus to Marcus Junius Brutus the Elder and Servilia.
Brutus' father is executed by Pompey during the civil wars; Brutus is later adopted by his uncle Quintus Servilius Caepio.
Brutus serves as an assistant to his uncle Cato in Cyprus, gaining administrative experience.
Brutus joins Pompey's side against Caesar in the civil war, despite Pompey having executed his father.
After Pompey's defeat at Pharsalus, Caesar pardons Brutus and welcomes him into his circle.
Caesar appoints Brutus as governor of Cisalpine Gaul.
Brutus serves as urban praetor; joins the conspiracy against Caesar led by Cassius.
Assassination of Julius Caesar on the Ides of March (March 15). Brutus is among the principal assassins.
Brutus flees Rome and goes to Athens, then to Macedonia and the eastern provinces.
Brutus and Cassius assemble a large army and confront Antony and Octavian at Philippi.
First Battle of Philippi: Brutus' forces defeat Octavian's wing, but Cassius, believing the battle lost, commits suicide.
Second Battle of Philippi: Brutus is decisively defeated and commits suicide.
